purpose: S4 for batch 4: the first-public minute of each release in the fourth batch, taken from the public wire page, and what was found on the way. config/m5-phase1b-events.json now holds nine events built from it in the dry-run state after the twenty-nine of batches 1 to 3: sealed, no attestations, so each quarantines on FIRST_PUBLIC_TIME_UNVERIFIED until the owner attests it. The tenth release, ASMB's, was made at the bell and is put aside for the owner's word. Nothing here is a price, a return or a label.

permission.read_as: Batch 4 only: the public pages of the releases of the ten candidates listed below on Business Wire, GlobeNewswire, PR Newswire or Accesswire, or on the issuer's own newsroom, to take each release's first-public minute, and a check for a separate same-day release. In the built-in browser, in browser memory only; the URL, the displayed minute and a short excerpt are kept. No web-search tool, no price or quote page, no filing. It carries no push and no other download; later batches ask again.

reading.what: The ten releases' pages and company searches on GlobeNewswire, Business Wire and PR Newswire (each issuer's wire is the one its earlier events in the repository used, except The RealReal, whose second-quarter release is on PR Newswire), and Take-Two's own investor-relations press-release list and release page, which gave no release minute; held in browser memory only; the URL, the displayed minute, the page's machine-readable time and the same-day check results are kept. No filing was opened: EDGAR's acceptance times come from the archived SEC lists already in the repository. Listings were read through short extractions of the dates, times and titles wanted, so as to see as little else as possible.
reading.what_was_seen_in_passing: Take-Two's investor page returned a sentence of the release (the conference call 'today at 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time') and, with a dateline extraction, a fragment of the company's net-bookings expectation; Business Wire's Take-Two listing showed titles of the company's other releases, one of them dated 2026-10-13 (a notice that it will report its next quarter's results); short datelines of other releases came back with their extractions. These are company-reported business content, not a price, a return or a label of any event.
reading.refused_or_missing: No site refused a page for permission. Business Wire's newsroom search answered 'Page Unavailable' (a reference id, no content) nine times, from three searches in quick succession onward, until about 45 minutes after my last attempt; its homepage loaded throughout. I did not route around it: I waited, then asked for one search at a time, and the Take-Two and KinderCare releases were read once it answered again. Two GlobeNewswire searches for The RealReal found nothing, because its release is on PR Newswire. The first batch call of GlobeNewswire searches stopped at its first action (the pane had to be reopened), so Aspen's search was loaded twice.

quarantined_before_the_spec.reason: Released at 16:00 ET, the regular-session close: nre/calendar.py's classify() returns bell_ambiguous for the instant of the close, which event_acquire.validate_spec() does not accept at minute precision, so no event spec can be built. ASMB 2026-05-07 was left quarantined, not excluded, for the same reason on the owner's word (reports/m5-phase1b-batch1-signoff-2026-10-09.json), as were Milestone 1's GALT and Milestone 2 step 2's PDFS 2025-08-07. The same disposition is proposed here; it needs the owner's word at the signoff. The owner's earlier decision on this candidate (kept with a caveat as the 8-K/A that stands for the 2026-08-13 release) does not decide the timing question.

Not a proof that nothing earlier was public: open-web research can show no discoverable earlier disclosure, not a negative.
